channel.title: Paperraft
channel.description: Research in efficient inference and AI agents, ranked by independent GitHub implementations instead of citations or stars. Papers above the attention threshold are deliberately excluded.

item.title: More with Less: Efficient Parallel Scientific Code Translation via an Agent-Skill Workflow
item.description: This framework replaces fixed sequential translation pipelines with a coordinated multi-agent system that separates translation, compilation diagnosis, and execution validation, routing failures to targeted repair skills based on orchestrator verdicts. It incurs the complexity of deploying and coordinating three autonomous agents plus an offline LLM verifier, and while it reduces token costs, it requires infrastructure capable of running concurrent agent workflows. Adoption risks include residual false positives in correctness verification that evade both compiler checks and the offline LLM, as well as potential reliability gaps when translating domain-specific or proprietary HPC kernels not represented in the HeCBench evaluation suite. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Knowledge Distillation from Neural Networks to Differentiable Logic Networks
item.description: The method replaces training a differentiable logic network (DLN) classifier directly with a two-phase distillation procedure from a trained MLP teacher, which is discarded after training so inference retains the DLN's interpretability, sparsity, and very low gate-level cost. The cost is added training complexity: a two-phase loop and tuning of distillation weight and temperature, with four investigated variants including a joint hyperparameter-architecture search; inference cost and model size are essentially unchanged. The benefit is dataset-dependent (up to 15% balanced-accuracy gain, varying across the 20 tasks), DLNs still underperform conventional networks on several datasets, and the approach applies only to tabular classification where DLN architectures and their immature ecosystem are viable. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: distillation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: A Controlled Study of Models, Skills, Feedback, and Curriculum in Agentic Robotics
item.description: This is not a deployable technique but a controlled empirical study of how coding agents iteratively improve robot policies, replacing intuition-driven agent design with systematic ablation over model capability, skill priors, feedback structure, and curriculum. Adopting its findings costs nothing computationally but requires a robotics simulation environment and a coding-agent rollout pipeline to act on; the study itself ran 28K rollouts across 631 configurations, a scale infeasible on the reader's budget. Its conclusions can fail to transfer because they are derived from nine simulated manipulation tasks and may not generalize to other domains or to real-world hardware. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: ToolDex: An Ego-Exo Human Demonstration Dataset for Creative Physical Tool Use
item.description: ToolDex introduces a real-world multi-view human demonstration dataset for creative physical tool use, replacing reliance on simulation-based or simplified interaction benchmarks in embodied AI research. It costs significant capture infrastructure (synchronized egocentric plus eight exocentric cameras with dense hand, tool, and deformation annotations) and does not provide a deployable model or inference method for a constrained 24 GB GPU or API-based stack. For this reader it carries no direct production benefit: its value is in training and evaluating robot policies and 3D/4D reconstruction, which require robotics hardware and data pipelines the reader does not operate, and benchmark results may not transfer to their LLM-centric workloads. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: MongoBench: Do LLMs Know What a MongoDB Query Will Do?
item.description: MongoBench replaces reliance on query validity and final-answer correctness as proxies for whether an agent understands its own database queries, adding a dedicated consequence-prediction check with a real mongod oracle. It costs the engineering effort of running the released benchmark and oracle against your models, plus ongoing evaluation time; prepending rule sheets helps unevenly. Failures concentrate in semantic pitfalls such as range comparisons and null handling, and delegating execution to the model can silently diverge from the intended query unless outputs pass a canonical check. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: When Routine Operations Break Architectural Pattern Relationships in LLM Agent Harnesses
item.description: The method replaces ad hoc testing of LLM agent harnesses with a systematic procedure (PatternOps) that traces architectural pattern requirements to their providers and validates them under routine operations such as plugin reapplication or rule saving. It requires analysis of decision paths, state lifetimes, and operation sequences, which adds engineering overhead before deployment. After adoption, guardrails can silently fail if runtime operations alter the order or state that pattern relationships depend on, allowing prohibited actions to execute while all components appear active. 2 independent implementations, 2126 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: DARIC: A Position-Independent KV Cache Reuse System with Distribution-Aware Recomputation
item.description: DARIC replaces full prefix prefill (and prior recomputation-based cache-reuse methods such as CacheBlend-style approaches) for repeated long contexts by storing position-independent KV caches and recomputing only a subset of tokens selected by empirical KV-deviation distributions, with a lightweight architecture intended to integrate with standard inference engines like vLLM. Costs include storing and managing reusable KV caches per document chunk, added integration and token-selection logic in the serving stack, and a residual recomputation pass whose overhead depends on the selected token fraction. It can fail when prefix reuse patterns are rare (unique or non-overlapping queries yield no benefit), when the assumed deviation distribution does not hold for a given model or tokenizer, or when third-party APIs are used, since the method requires access to KV-cache internals unavailable through black-box endpoints. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: UniExit: A Unified Latency-Aware Early-Exit Runtime for Heterogeneous Edge AI
item.description: Replaces static, model-specific early-exit policies and fixed latency profiling with a unified runtime that treats CNN blocks and Transformer layers as stages, using runtime-state-aware latency prediction, cache-based reuse, trend-aware fallback, and CNN-specific exit stabilization. Costs include the overhead of online latency prediction, cache management, integration engineering for heterogeneous models, and potential accuracy degradation from premature exits under aggressive budgets. Can fail when runtime state prediction is inaccurate under bursty load, when model-specific quality mechanisms conflict with the unified policy, or when the edge hardware lacks sufficient sensors for reliable state estimation. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Beyond the Grid: Continuous Dictionary Pursuit for Interpretable Signal Decomposition
item.description: It replaces discrete matching pursuit, sparse coding with gridded dictionaries, and opaque neural decomposers with greedy gradient-based optimization over continuous differentiable atom families (periodic, trend, transient, discontinuous). Cost is per-signal iterative optimization with data-driven priors and spectral sharpness annealing, plus a tuned atom budget and residual stopping criterion, rather than a single forward pass or one dictionary lookup. It can fail when true components lie outside the library, when greedy selection mis-isolates overlapping or nonstationary components, and when annealing, priors, or stopping thresholds are mis-set, since the 1% recovery and forecasting gains are conditional on library expressibility and evaluated workloads. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: test.

item.title: RoleWalk: training-free structural embeddings for directed graphs that transfer across graphs
item.description: RoleWalk replaces learned or whole-graph-dependent structural role embeddings (struc2vec, Role2Vec, GraphWave, Digraphwave) with a training-free, neighbourhood-local embedding built from short lazy random walks, which makes coordinates comparable across graphs. It costs only CPU time (one core suffices for million-node graphs), introduces pruning error that is bounded by a per-node certificate, and requires no GPU, training pipeline, or labelled data. It can fail when node roles depend on graph structure beyond the fixed walk radius, when the target task rewards neighbour-identity rather than structural features, or on graphs where the lazy-walk assumptions (e.g., very sparse or degenerate degree distributions) make the characteristic-function representation uninformative. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Fused-Softmax for efficient quantized attention
item.description: The method replaces the standard vector-unit softmax inside attention with a reformulated, approximated softmax whose dominant operations are folded into the attention GEMMs, shifting work to matrix cores. It costs an implementation tied to AMD CDNA 4 hardware (MI355X) via the AITER library, requires MXFP8/6/4 quantization of attention operands, and adds approximation error that the authors claim stays below the GEMM quantization error floor. It can fail on non-AMD hardware where no kernel exists, and accuracy may degrade on workloads whose quantization error floor is lower than the video-generation model validated in the paper. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: attention and kernels. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Cross-Layer TopK: Dynamically Allocating Sparsity Across Layers in Transcoders
item.description: Cross-Layer TopK replaces the JumpReLU penalty-based sparsity recipe and per-layer fixed TopK budgets for training cross-layer transcoders (CLTs) with a single whole-model L0 budget allocated dynamically across layers during training. The cost is a custom training and sparse-decoding stack, plus dependence on a base model large enough to need a CLT; this is a research training cost, not a serving optimization, and open weights are available. It can fail to transfer to different base-model architectures, the interpretability gains do not reduce inference cost or latency in the reader's production serving path, and sparse-decoding speedups depend on a fixed per-token budget that the team's pipeline must support. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: DUET: Dual-Sparse Inference for Block Diffusion Language Models
item.description: Duet replaces full-prefix attention and full-block propagation at every denoising step in block diffusion language models with a reused compact historical KV subset and query pruning that sends only likely-updated positions through the suffix Transformer layers, all without retraining. It costs implementation complexity in KV selection and shallow-layer update prediction, plus a modest accuracy risk that the paper reports as small but nonzero. It can fail if attention concentration or cross-step stability does not hold on the reader's prompts, if the underlying model is an autoregressive rather than a block-diffusion LM, or if predicted update positions miss tokens that actually needed deep computation. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: sparsity and pruning. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Nudging Decision Models: Do Digital Nudges Steer Fast, Generation-Free AI Agents?
item.description: Replaces text-generating LLM agents for option-selection steps with non-generative decision models that output a choice directly, cutting inference latency and API cost. Costs include adopting a distinct model class (Jev, Decision-1, d1) that may not be accessible via standard APIs, plus added behavioral fragility. Can fail by being steered unintentionally: defaults and social-influence signals dominate choices in a System 1 pattern, risking compliance, fairness, and robustness problems in production. 1 independent implementation, 135 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Towards an Autonomous AI Steward for Large-Scale Physics Experiments: Integrating Causal Diagnostics, RAG, and Conformal Prediction
item.description: The method replaces manual alarm triage and ad hoc expert handoffs with an asynchronous causal diagnostics engine feeding a DAG of ReAct agents grounded by RAG and bounded by conformal prediction. It costs a hybrid C++ and Python service stack, continuous access to live slow-control and DAQ streams, curated institutional memory for retrieval, and nontrivial integration work with experiment-specific run control and HitL guardrails. It can fail if causal discovery misidentifies root causes under non-stationary machine states, retrieval is incomplete or stale, conformal guarantees are misread as action correctness, or the shadow-tested workflow does not transfer to smaller production systems. 1 independent implementation, 135 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Robust Deep Prototype Classifiers via Lipschitz Training
item.description: The method replaces an unconstrained embedding network feeding a linear, SVM, or GLVQ classification head with a Lipschitz-constrained embedding paired with a prototype-based head, extending the prototype margin certificate into input space as an ε/L robustness bound. It costs additional training complexity from sampling-based Lipschitz enforcement, constrains the network's capacity, and requires retraining the embedding rather than dropping into an existing pipeline. It can fail because the Lipschitz property is enforced empirically by sampling rather than by construction, so the reported robustness is not certified and may not hold against stronger or adaptive attacks, and gains are demonstrated only on small image benchmarks (MNIST, CIFAR-10, Imagenette-160). 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: SafeOrchestrate: Runtime Checked Intent-Driven Orchestration for Cyber-Physical Systems
item.description: The method replaces unconstrained LLM-to-MCP tool use with a pipeline that derives atomic goals from natural-language intent, generates runtime-checkable LTL-style specifications, grounds them to WoT Thing Description affordances, and verifies candidate actions against SMT-backed safety constraints before execution. The cost is added system complexity and latency: the pipeline requires an LTL generation step, a grounding step, and an SMT solver in the execution loop, plus engineering effort to maintain the specification and constraint models. Failure modes include incorrect or incomplete LTL specifications generated by the LLM, grounding errors when affordances are ambiguous, and SMT models that are over-permissive or over-restrictive, which can respectively admit unsafe actions or block legitimate ones. 3 independent implementations, 2244 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Enabling Privacy-Preserving Natural Language Access to Industrial Smart Meter Data
item.description: Replaces manual SQL authoring and cloud-based LLM APIs that violate data privacy constraints with a local, schema-agnostic multi-agent pipeline. Costs increased architectural complexity, latency from agent communication overhead, and higher local inference compute compared to single-agent or direct API calls. Small models may fail at complex reasoning tasks, and the accuracy benefits of full orchestration diminish at frontier scale, risking unnecessary overhead if components are not selectively enabled. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Tracybot: Preserving Developer Intent by Tracing Agent-Generated Code to Prompts
item.description: Tracybot replaces the undocumented status quo in which agent-assisted design decisions remain in transient chat sessions disconnected from the committed code they produced. Its cost is workflow overhead: developers must structure work as Tasklets inside a VS Code/Git integration, and the capture instrumentation adds process friction without measurable engineering gains claimed in the paper. Adoption can fail if line-level mappings drift under subsequent manual edits or refactors, if developers bypass the tooling, or if the seven-participant focus group and 24-participant survey do not generalize to the reader's team practices. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: MINE: Entropy-coded Memory-efficient Inference for Large Language Models
item.description: MINE replaces standard quantized-weight storage and dequantization kernels in single-stream inference with a lossless entropy coding scheme (dtANS-LLM) that compresses the non-uniform weight distribution and integrates into vLLM as a plugin. It costs per-tensor and per-GPU auto-tuning of compression hyper-parameters, adds entropy-decoding compute to each weight fetch, and demonstrated results depend on a specific EntQuant checkpoint format rather than arbitrary quantized models. Adoption can fail if the reader's models lack compatible checkpoints, if decode overhead erases the compression gain on different GPUs, or if the workload batches requests, since the benefit targets strictly single-stream, memory-bound decoding. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Incentive Pathologies in a Live LLM Agent Arena: An Empirical Study of Concentration, Reward-Rule Implementation Discrepancy, and Network Dilution
item.description: The study replaces assumption-driven incentive design with empirical auditing of a live agent arena, using concentration metrics, code-level reconstruction, and trend tests to expose gaps between announced and implemented reward rules. It costs substantial observational infrastructure—nine days of logging across 22 agents and ~96,000 reasoning nodes—plus reverse-engineering effort that most small teams cannot replicate on third-party platforms. Adoption can fail because the findings are specific to one arena with bundled, non-isolated interventions, the headline Gini result is statistically inconclusive, and the audit detects problems without providing a validated remediation method. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: From LoRA to Language: Recovering Skill Documents from Adapters
item.description: The method replaces opaque, non-portable LoRA skill adapters with readable, editable, model-agnostic skill documents regenerated either by a small writer model trained over the adapted base or by an agent that diffs base-versus-adapter behavior. It costs training data and compute for the writer (or extra inference runs for the differential agent), adds a pipeline stage, and yields a document that captures only a fraction of the original instructions. It fails when the adapter was trained on behavior alone rather than on the document (1-2% instruction recovery), when the adapter's behavior is already guessable from the base model (a reward loop without the adapter performs equally well), and weight-only reading approaches transmit about one bit. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: distillation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Nebula: Distributed Position-Independent Caching for LLM Serving
item.description: Nebula replaces prefix-caching-centric distributed KV reuse with a cluster serving framework that treats position-independent cache segments as first-class objects, adding remote PIC reuse, parallel prefill, and cluster-wide cache management. Its cost is substantial serving-system complexity: optimistic accounting plus event-driven state tracking, adaptive PC/PIC capacity splitting via ghost-hit feedback, and a unified prefill completion-time model for parallelism and placement. It can fail when the assumed multi-segment reuse pattern is weak, when optimistic cluster accounting becomes inaccurate under fast-changing cache state, or when KV transfer and scheduling overheads outweigh prefill savings on a single-GPU deployment. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: e-means: outperforming k-means (in one-tenth the epochs)
item.description: e-means replaces Lloyd's k-means iteration (and often k-means++ initialization benefits) with an exponential moving average mini-batch update rule, plus scaling laws that set decay rate and batch size without a hyperparameter sweep, for clustering, quantization, and data curation workloads. The cost is adopting a new implementation and its optimizer-like machinery rather than a mature library routine, with EMA decay interacting with batch size if the prescribed rule is not followed. It can fail if the scaling-law formula does not transfer to embedding distributions or cluster counts outside the evaluated regimes, or if downstream pipelines depend on exact Lloyd-style centroid semantics. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: test.

item.title: StockASkill: A Local-First AgentSkill for Intelligent Stock Selection
item.description: Replaces remote API-dependent quantitative data retrieval and screening with a local DuckDB OLAP layer exposing a JSON tool-calling interface for LLM agents. Costs include maintaining a multi-market historical dataset locally, implementing the factor, optimization, and lot-quantization pipeline, and accepting that the reported Sharpe and Calmar figures come from the authors' own backtests rather than live trading. Can fail through survivorship or data-quality issues in the local store, backtest overfitting that does not survive live execution, and market-specific assumptions such as 100-share board lots that limit transferability. 1 independent implementation, 139 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Transformer-FSQ: Discrete Latents for Extreme KV-Cache Compression
item.description: The method replaces standard key and value projections with a finite scalar quantisation (FSQ) bottleneck, storing packed discrete integer codes per token instead of full-precision KV entries, with no per-token quantisation metadata. Converting a pretrained transformer requires training only the new projections on roughly 0.25 tokens per original parameter, plus adoption of a custom fused Triton decoding kernel. Accuracy can degrade outside the evaluated retrieval setting: the paper shows existing baselines fail beyond moderate ratios, and the method's gains are demonstrated on RULER long-context retrieval for Qwen-family base models 0.6B-8B, not on general generation quality or instruction-tuned chat workloads. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Encoding Memory in World Models with Test-Time Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
item.description: The method replaces reliance on purely contextual or architectural memory in model-based RL by updating world model parameters with gradient descent at test time so each episode has a distinct model. Its cost is extra test-time optimization, added implementation complexity, and a workflow tied to RL world-model training rather than standard LLM serving. It can fail if test-time adaptation is unstable, overfits the current episode, or does not transfer to production LLM inference settings under a 24 GB budget. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Steerable Multi-Objective Group-Relative Preference Optimization with Jointly Trained Low-Rank Adapters
item.description: LambdaMix replaces training and storing one specialist RL policy per objective weighting (e.g., a set of GRPO checkpoints) with a single run that jointly trains one LoRA adapter per objective over a frozen base, mixed at inference by a preference vector. It costs a group-relative online RL training run (comparable to GRPO, which itself requires reward models, rollout infrastructure, and tuning), plus serving-time logic to combine adapters and weight normalized rewards. It can fail if the preference-conditioned mixture does not interpolate reliably on your objective pair, if the frozen base model limits reachable trade-offs, or if normalized reward weighting produces unstable gradients on objectives with different reward scales. 2 independent implementations, 2241 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: NAVE: A Normalized, Adaptive Conformer for Antarctic Whale Vocalization Detection
item.description: NAVE replaces a two-stage detector (boundary-proposal network plus post-processing parameter search) with a single Conformer using per-bin complex mean subtraction, a PCEN channel, a frequency-dynamic convolutional stem, and a duration-matched convolution kernel. The cost is a task-specific architecture and input pipeline tied to known call duration and frequency bands, plus per-class threshold tuning, with no reported latency or memory figures. It can fail on target events whose duration or frequency characteristics differ from the baked-in inductive biases, and the leave-one-site-out gains may not transfer to non-acoustic or non-Antarctic domains. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: Breaking the Privacy Promise: Gradient Inversion Attacks on Federated Low-Rank Adapted Vision Transformers
item.description: The technique replaces standard gradient inversion attacks (such as GIAS) with a spatially anchored generative framework that introduces server-prescribed trainable positional embeddings during client fine-tuning to create spatial anchors for reconstruction. It requires modifying client-side ViT architectures to include these trainable positional embeddings and increases server-side computational cost for the generative inversion process. Success depends on client adoption of the modified architecture; without client-side implementation of the positional embedding changes, the spatial anchoring mechanism fails and reconstruction quality degrades to baseline levels. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Attend at the Right Resolution: Head-Adaptive Sparse Attention via Query-Key Interaction Structure
item.description: HASA replaces dense attention and fixed-heuristic training-free sparse attention with head-specific selection: each head's query-key operator is compressed to an effective-rank response space, tokens are merged by directional coherence, and exact attention runs on the original KV states of selected regions. It requires no retraining but adds per-head singular-spectrum analysis, region-merging logic, and non-standard attention kernels or routing code, increasing inference-path complexity. It can fail if pretrained heads exhibit diffuse interaction structure (raising effective rank and erasing sparsity), if region merging discards critical tokens on out-of-distribution inputs, or if the 11.9% of missed attention mass degrades tasks sensitive to long-range rare dependencies; realized speedup also depends on hardware-efficient sparse kernels, which a single 24 GB GPU deployment may not yet have. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: attention and kernels. Recommendation: test.

item.title: MemoryDojo: Benchmarking Poisoning Through LLM Agent Memory
item.description: Replaces ad-hoc or absent red-teaming of agent memory with a standardized benchmark (155 multi-session trajectories, five memory systems) for tracing how poisoned instructions persist and resurface across sessions. Costs are benchmark-integration and evaluation engineering effort, plus any API or local inference spend for running trajectories; the benchmark itself is an evaluation harness, not a defense, so adopting it adds testing overhead without reducing attack surface. It can fail to transfer if the reader's production memory architecture or threat model differs from the five systems and four domains covered, and a strong result on this benchmark does not guarantee robustness against the paper's own memory-aware poison optimization or future adaptive attacks. 2 independent implementations, 2126 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Language as Trait, Politeness as Strategy: Controlled Tests of Linguistic Effects in LLM Social-Deduction Agents
item.description: The paper tests whether rewriting utterances for linguistic range or politeness changes how other agents judge and act, but finds no reliable effect. It replaces ad-hoc assumptions about tone with controlled replay experiments using the LURK Werewolf framework. Costs include implementing a replay harness and running many controlled trials. The approach can fail if speech-act separation is imperfect or if results do not generalize beyond the specific game setting. 1 independent implementation, 135 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: AnimWeb-Bench: Benchmarking Animated Webpage Code Generation from Videos
item.description: AnimWeb-Bench replaces ad hoc or screenshot-only evaluation of webpage code generation with a video-grounded, two-dimensional protocol: Static Appearance Fidelity on aligned keyframes and Animation Fidelity tracking component position, size, velocity, and appearance. It costs only evaluation compute (video rendering, keyframe alignment, and component tracking across frames) plus integration into an existing test harness; it does not reduce inference or training cost. It can fail if the automated component-tracking metrics diverge from human judgment on real production pages, if its 124-page sample is unrepresentative of the reader's domain, or if teams overfit prompting strategies to the benchmark rather than to actual design requirements. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Knowing When to Intervene: Causal Evaluation of AI Agents
item.description: The method replaces static benchmark scores and ad-hoc auditing rules with a framework that estimates the causal effect of intervening at specific points in an agent's trajectory. It costs a randomized data collection phase where interventions are applied stochastically to logged trajectories, adding statistical complexity and requiring offline policy evaluation tooling. It can fail if the logged trajectories lack sufficient coverage of the intervention states (positivity violation) or if unmeasured confounders bias the estimated causal effects. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: When Instruction Files Go Stale: Documentation Debt and Hidden Cost in Coding Agents
item.description: Manual periodic review of repository instruction files (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md) replaces the implicit assumption that documentation remains accurate. It costs engineering time to audit these files against codebase evolution and adds latency to maintenance workflows. It can fail if reviews become rote checklists that miss semantic drift—where instructions remain technically correct but no longer reflect architectural intent—while the paper shows agents will still follow demonstrably stale paths, wasting tool calls on obsolete operations. 0 independent implementations, 10 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Agents on the Patch Path: Mining AI-Associated Security Remediation in GitHub Security Advisories
item.description: This is an empirical measurement study, not a deployable technique; it replaces ad hoc anecdote with a local-Git mining pipeline that detects coding-agent attribution in commits referenced by GitHub Security Advisories, but it offers nothing to adopt in a production stack. The cost to replicate is modest (local repository cloning plus heuristic attribution rules), yet the pipeline's value is research-grade rather than operational. Its detection heuristics can fail through false positives from repository-level evidence alone and false negatives when agents leave no explicit attribution, so its 469-candidate count is a lower-bound estimate with noisy edges. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: BitDecoding-FP4: Native FP4 KV Cache Decoding via Algorithm-System Co-Design
item.description: Replaces BF16/FP16 KV cache attention with end-to-end NVFP4/MXFP4 decoding, combining dual-residual query quantization, underflow-aware probability scaling, and outlier-aware key quantization with fused transposed-softmax kernels on paged caches. The cost is substantial implementation complexity: accuracy depends on Hadamard rotation, scale search, and static smoothing, while throughput depends on custom FP4 Tensor Core kernels. It can fail on hardware without native FP4 support (the 2.4-3.0x result is B300-specific), on workloads where its quantization assumptions (e.g., RL rollouts, MoE/MLA variants) are untested, or if the fixed-scale error budget exceeds tolerance on domains not in its evaluation. 0 independent implementations, 12 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: How far does a hash-only sender go? A pre-registered map of sender memory versus bits for short text messages
item.description: Replaces a trained in-domain PPM sender with a hash-only sender plus receiver LM search. Costs 18.4 bits more per message than PPM order 1 under the pre-registered endpoint and loses in airtime on all five priced links due to acknowledgement and fallback frames. Wider receiver search recovers about half of failures at roughly three minutes receiver time per failure while still losing airtime on four of five links. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: CodeQuant2: Enhanced Outlier Mitigation and Adaptive Clustering for Low-Precision LRMs
item.description: Replaces standard low-bit weight quantization (e.g., GPTQ/AWQ-style calibration) with rotation-and-scaling outlier mitigation, clustering-based codebooks with per-layer adaptive bit allocation, and calibration samples matched to early reasoning decoding statistics. Costs implementation complexity: it depends on a custom LUT CUDA kernel, per-layer codebook tuning, and a calibration pipeline that must capture early-token activation states, plus lookup overhead that may not reach the reported speedup on all hardware. Can fail when reasoning activation distributions differ from the calibration data, when small model sizes make the LUT kernel overhead dominate, or when the custom kernel is unmaintained for the reader's deployment stack. 0 independent implementations, 125 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Measuring Model-Specific Alignment Drift in LLM-Based Opinion Dynamics
item.description: The method replaces the assumption that an LLM agent's behavior is fully determined by its prompt with a fixed psychometric instrument that quantifies stance across repeated discussion rounds, independent of any dynamics model. It costs repeated multi-round agent conversations plus per-round instrument scoring across candidate models, which is feasible on third-party APIs but adds evaluation latency and token spend before any simulation is trusted. It can fail because findings are model-specific and may not transfer across model versions, issues, or population sizes, so a model validated today can drift differently after a provider update. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: SLATE: A Large-Scale Benchmark for Long-Horizon API Selection in E-commerce Tool Use
item.description: SLATE replaces small-tool, single-step, or LLM-as-a-judge tool-use evaluations with a ~1,000-tool e-commerce benchmark using a deterministic simulator and an automatic end-to-end task-success metric that accepts valid alternative trajectories. Adopting it costs the effort of integrating the released simulator and harness, and its e-commerce tool library does not directly measure performance on an organization's own API stack. It can fail as a proxy if internal APIs, procedure distributions, or failure modes differ substantially from the benchmark's synthetic e-commerce domain, and it evaluates models rather than improving them. 1 independent implementation, 20 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Dory1.0-4B: A Looped Normalized-GPT
item.description: Replaces fixed-depth inference and the need to deploy larger checkpoints with a single 4B checkpoint whose shared recurrent block is applied a variable number of times, trading extra latent compute for accuracy instead of longer outputs or bigger models. Costs additional latency and compute per generated token roughly proportional to loop count, requires inference-stack support for looped execution (non-standard serving code), and the reported gains stem from a 6-trillion-token pre-training run plus NVFP4 training and RLVR post-training that the reader cannot replicate. Loop benefits are benchmark- and task-dependent (largest on coding, agentic, long-context), may not transfer to the reader's workload, and tooling for last-loop-only KV caching and difficulty-aware loop routing may be immature outside the authors' release. 0 independent implementations, 15 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: test.

item.title: WASP-Mem: Let Agent Organize Procedural Memory. Human Spend Effort on Diagnosis
item.description: WASP-Mem replaces static, hand-built agent harnesses and prescriptive memory schemas with wiki pages that the agent itself distills from execution traces and feedback, consolidating reusable actions and recovery strategies without any model training. The cost is ongoing trace ingestion and synthesis via LLM calls (third-party APIs are sufficient), plus the key operational investment: human diagnosis of failed traces, which the paper shows is what drives sustained gains. It can fail when no human diagnosis capacity exists (self-judgment refinement is markedly weaker), when the target procedures lack repeated trace volume to consolidate, and because results are validated on a single benchmark and may not transfer to proprietary enterprise workflows. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: HybridSpec: Throughput-Aware Speculative Decoding for Hybrid GDN-MoE Models
item.description: HybridSpec replaces fixed-length speculative verification in DFlash-style decoding with GPU-side adaptive verification-length selection, early MoE routing correction, and block-parallel GDN kernels with single-launch state reconstruction. It costs custom GDN kernel implementation, draft-side acceptance estimation, on-GPU latency measurement, and added verification-pipeline complexity, and it is tied to hybrid GDN-MoE architectures. It can fail if acceptance estimates are miscalibrated, if router correction rejects useful tokens or admits wasted ones, if kernels are unavailable for the deployment stack, or if the reader's models are dense rather than GDN-MoE. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: ScienceVision: Can AI Observe and Reason Like a Scientist?
item.description: This is a 250-question expert-reviewed benchmark that replaces ad hoc, discipline-specific 3D evaluation protocols with a unified VQA harness supporting native 3D artifacts, MCP-based inspection tools, and rendered 2D baselines. It costs nothing to deploy as a model, but adopting its findings implies building agentic file/code-execution and MCP tooling pipelines, which adds integration complexity. Results can fail to transfer because the benchmark is small (50 questions per domain), models score at most 0.53, and tool-access harnesses may not match a given production stack. 1 independent implementation, 37 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Say Less, Mean Better: Training-Free Verbosity Control for Language Models
item.description: Replaces naive prompting-based conciseness and aggressive early stopping with a decoding-time framework combining uncertainty-aware stop-token adjustment and structural completeness guardrails, requiring no fine-tuning or auxiliary models. Costs a modest quality reduction (8.04 versus 8.42 out of 10) and added decoding-logic complexity in the inference path. Can fail when completeness checks misfire on atypical response structures, when the uncertainty signal is unreliable for a given model or domain, and the evaluation is limited to three models and 330 questions, so gains may not transfer to all workloads or API-based models where logits access is restricted. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient architectures. Recommendation: test.

item.title: LoopKV: Loop-Aware KV Cache Compression for Serving Looped Transformers
item.description: LoopKV replaces uniform-bit KV cache quantization (e.g., KIVI-4) with per-(loop,layer) precision allocation—4-bit, 2-bit, or cross-loop reuse—based on an offline sensitivity profile, executed via a fused vLLM kernel. Costs include a one-time offline profiling step, a custom fused kernel, and plan storage; it applies only to looped transformers that keep separate KV per loop, such as Ouro. It can fail if damage-additivity assumptions break on other models or workloads, if skipping low-attention values compounds errors across loops, or if the target deployment does not use looped architectures at all. 0 independent implementations, 15 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: HyPAIC: Personal AI Computer with High Bandwidth Flash for High Performance Trillion-Parameter LLM Inference
item.description: HyPAIC replaces LPDDR-only unified memory in personal AI computers with a split design storing read-only model weights in high-bandwidth flash (HBF) and mutable runtime data (KV cache) in LPDDR. The cost is a hardware platform that does not yet exist commercially: HBF specifications are still evolving, and the design must manage HBF's access latency, limited write endurance, page-level access granularity, and unresolved power and cooling demands. The approach can fail because all results are simulation-based, prefetching may not hide latency for irregular access patterns, and write endurance constrains the read-only placement assumption. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: RGDM: Robust Graph Diffusion Model
item.description: RGDM replaces conventional graph adversarial defenses (adversarial retraining, edge pruning, graph purification) with a generative approach: a robust graph autoencoder with edge selection and low-rank latent regularization, plus a latent diffusion model, synthesizes clean labeled nodes and edges that are merged into the corrupted graph before GNN training. The cost is training and tuning two models (autoencoder plus latent diffusion) per graph domain, which is feasible on a single 24 GB GPU for citation-scale graphs but adds a full generative pipeline, hyperparameter burden, and inference-time generation step relative to simpler defenses. It can fail when the adversarial corruption shifts the latent distribution beyond what the low-rank regularization captures, when generated structures inject label noise that degrades clean accuracy, or when the evaluation setting (semi-supervised node classification on benchmark graphs) does not transfer to larger or differently attacked production graphs. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: test.

item.title: What Remains in Sight? Autoregressive Video Decoding as Representation-Guided Context Rewriting
item.description: ReCR replaces implicit past-context selection (recent windows, compressed caches, external memory) in autoregressive video decoding with an explicit training-free selection of history units guided by internal decoder representations, mapped onto a compact causal axis before each block is decoded. It costs additional inference-time computation for representation extraction and selection scoring, and implementation complexity to expose decoder internals, while keeping the visible-token budget unchanged. It can fail if the backbone does not expose suitable internal representations, if the selection heuristics (global-state match, redundancy avoidance, boundary coverage, spatial diversity) misfire on the target domain, or if the quality gain does not materialize on workloads whose degradation mode differs from the evaluated benchmarks. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: When the Consumer Is an Agent: Execution-Grounded Service-Level Agreements
item.description: The technique replaces the LLM agent's self-reported task completion with an independent control plane that observes a deadline-bound service-state predicate, admits or rejects completion, and directs recovery. It costs an additional control-plane component, state-predicate instrumentation per service, and deadline monitoring that can delay or reject legitimately completed work when observation lags. It can fail when state predicates are mis-specified, when observability of the target service is itself delayed or incomplete, or when healthy tasks are terminated as unverified due to monitoring faults rather than task faults. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: failure recovery. Recommendation: test.

item.title: What Does 4-Bit Microscaling Cost a Wearable Activity Recognizer?
item.description: The technique replaces full-precision (FP32/FP16) or 8-bit integer quantization of weights and activations with 4-bit block-scaled floating-point formats (MXFP4, NVFP4) to cut model storage and memory traffic on-device. Costs: simulated 4-bit weights-plus-activations quantization degrades accuracy (0.75 F1 points with NVFP4, 5.14 with MXFP4), and MXFP4's reference scale-rounding-down rule clips block maxima unless corrected to round-up plus an 8-bit FP scale. What can fail: results are simulated rather than measured on real 4-bit hardware for a single small 1D CNN on one dataset, MXFP4 degrades sharply under naive scale selection, and gains may not transfer to other models, tasks, or actual silicon. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: quantization. Recommendation: test.

item.title: DoGNAVY-Exploit: Harnessing Parallel Open-Weight Agents for Stage-Aware Vulnerability Exploitation
item.description: It replaces single-agent long-horizon exploitation with a milestone-decomposed, planner-executor-controller harness that injects stage-relevant knowledge, runs parallel attack routes, and consolidates verified findings in shared structured memory. The cost is substantial orchestration complexity, multiple concurrent agents per task with associated token and compute spend, and engineering of milestones, expert knowledge modules, and evidence-based acceptance logic. It can fail outside controlled benchmarks: reported gains come from Cybench, CVE-Bench, and ExploitGym, ablations show each component matters (so partial adoption may underperform), and the approach depends on specific open-weight models whose availability and behavior may change. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: LIRA: A More Interpretable Dynamic Loss-Informed Rank Allocation for Low-Rank Adaptation
item.description: LIRA replaces fixed-rank or heuristically reallocated LoRA with periodic rank reallocation scored by a second-order estimate of the local loss perturbation from recent LoRA-factor movements, while keeping standard (A,B) adapters and matched rank budgets. It costs periodic rank-scoring and reallocation overhead during training, plus implementation complexity beyond stock LoRA, though the Trajectory EMA variant reduces estimation cost relative to the Fisher-based variant. It can fail if the second-order approximation misestimates layer importance on tasks or architectures beyond RoBERTa-base GLUE, and its reported gains are validated only at that small scale. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: LIBRA: Programmatic Induction of Executable Tool Libraries
item.description: LIBRA replaces flat tool retrieval with a pre-built executable library that maps prerequisite dependencies between tools. It requires an offline phase where an LLM proposes tool contracts which are then validated in a sandbox, incurring upfront computational and engineering overhead before query time. The approach can fail if the LLM hallucinates invalid tool contracts during the proposal phase or if the runtime environment diverges from the sandbox, causing the induced library to become stale or incorrect. 3 independent implementations, 26 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Agentic Behavior Engineering: A Design-by-Contract Methodology for Specifying, Verifying, and Governing Enterprise AI Agents
item.description: ABE replaces prompt- or model-centric ad hoc testing with version-controlled behavior contracts, scenario libraries, and per-scenario pass^k release gating, treating observable behavior as the engineering artifact. It costs specification and scenario-authoring effort plus ongoing maintenance of contract-referenced tests, runtime policies, and telemetry, but requires no extra compute, cluster, or model training and works with third-party APIs. It can fail if contracts are incomplete or mis-specified, if scenario coverage misses real production distributions, or if pass^k gating on non-deterministic outputs yields flaky gates that erode team trust in the process. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: SlackBench: Benchmarking Agents on Collaborative Projects Grounded in Real Code Repositories
item.description: SlackBench replaces ad hoc or synthetic-agent evaluation with 140 queries over reproducible, privacy-preserving reenactments of real research projects, requiring joint reasoning over Slack-style conversations, GitHub repository state, and documents. It costs the effort of setting up the benchmark environments and agent harnesses and running agents through them (API inference costs if frontier models are used), and it measures rather than improves any system. It can fail to transfer: results on academic-project reenactments may not predict agent performance on the reader's own workplace data, channels, and codebases, and scores depend heavily on the harness configuration. 0 independent implementations, 20 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Iterated creation, grading, and revision of data science projects by language models
item.description: The technique replaces single-pass agent execution with a loop in which a writer LLM produces a data science project, a grader LLM scores it, and the writer revises across three rounds. It costs roughly three times the API tokens, latency, and tool-call budget of a single pass, plus the engineering to execute submissions and manage grading, with no local GPU requirement. It can fail because much of the measured improvement is grader noise, self-grading is biased upward, gains are highly model- and pairing-dependent, and weaker graders do not improve stronger writers. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Easy Multi-Precision Acceleration via Vectorization
item.description: The method replaces hand-written, hardware-specific low-level kernels (CUDA/assembly or per-generation tuning) with high-level vectorized matrix operations that map onto accelerator BLAS/FFT libraries across precisions and hardware generations. The cost is dependence on the quality of the underlying vendor libraries, limited control for irregular or fused operations, and potential sub-peak results for workloads outside dense linear algebra and FFT convolution. It can fail when a workload is dominated by custom fused kernels, small or irregular shapes, or when lower-precision paths introduce accuracy loss the application cannot tolerate. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: attention and kernels. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Role-based Effectiveness of an Epistemic Uncertainty Estimate in Training Models for Semantic Segmentation of 3D LiDAR Point Clouds
item.description: The method replaces standard deterministic segmentation training (baseline ANN, PointNet++, RandLA-Net) with training that injects a generatively estimated epistemic uncertainty signal, either as an additional input feature or as a per-sample confidence weight in the loss. It costs an extra uncertainty-estimation stage per point cloud plus modest training-time overhead, with no reported inference latency penalty and no large hardware requirement. It can fail where the uncertainty estimate is poorly calibrated: the error-uncertainty alignment (PAvPU) improved in only half of the configurations, so misweighted or misleading uncertainty can leave accuracy unchanged or degrade calibration. 1 independent implementation, 50 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Distinguishing Initial-Condition and Model Error Using Machine-Learning Weather Models
item.description: This method replaces traditional data assimilation with differentiable optimization that jointly adjusts initial conditions and model parameters (via LoRA) using a second weather model as a supervisor to disentangle error sources. It requires access to pre-trained weather models (GraphCast, Pangu-Weather), reanalysis datasets, and significant compute for gradient-based optimization, which exceeds typical 24 GB GPU constraints for full-scale atmospheric models. Failure modes include overfitting to specific reanalysis data, high sensitivity to hyperparameters, and poor generalization to out-of-distribution weather events. 0 independent implementations, 3 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: GaussianRenderFormer: Transformer-based Rendering of 3D Gaussian Splats
item.description: GaussianRenderFormer replaces the conventional rasterizer in a 3D Gaussian splatting pipeline with a transformer that maps Gaussian tokens and camera-ray patches directly to pixels. It costs a training run over 26,820 Objaverse objects and currently sacrifices substantial quality, reaching 38.08 dB PSNR versus 44.02 dB for standard rasterization of the same pruned inputs, with the gap traced to the view decoder rather than generalization. After adoption it can fail through under-training, a decoder bottleneck that requires auxiliary footprint information to partially close, and no demonstrated benefit over the mature rasterizer it replaces. 1 independent implementation, 1 star. Research area: other. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: LACS: Distribution-Sensitive Label-Agnostic Confidence Selection for Dynamic Data Pruning
item.description: LACS replaces fixed-quota or absolute-threshold data pruning during training with a distribution-relative rule that skips examples whose maximum predictive confidence exceeds a log-mean-exp reference plus a margin, requiring no labels or per-example gradients. The cost is an extra scoring forward pass per selection step in the current implementation, so backward sparsity does not yet yield wall-clock speedup, plus the risk of discarding confidently wrong examples that may be informative. It can fail when the confidence distribution is poorly calibrated, when removal thresholds interact badly with curriculum effects early in training, or when the scoring overhead outweighs the saved backward computation on small models. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: efficient training. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Route to Remember: Adaptive Memory Selection for LLM Agents
item.description: The method replaces per-query retrieval of accumulated textual memory with knowledge internalized into model weights via on-policy self-distillation, plus a verify-then-regenerate router that falls back to text memory when weight memory is uncertain. It costs a per-user or per-domain fine-tuning pipeline (teacher-student training of the same model), ongoing retraining as facts accumulate, and added routing complexity, though it reduces tokens read per query at inference. It can fail on episodic facts not yet distilled into weights, on stale knowledge after user data changes, and on router misjudgments that answer from weights when retrieval was needed. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Runway Characters: Serving a 57B Video Diffusion Transformer for Real-Time Conversation
item.description: The method recomputes whole-KV-cache work at write time (a ring cache with RoPE and FP8 quantization applied once per write, plus a delta rotation on position reset) instead of repeating it in every attention call, and fuses tensor-parallel all-reduce into the FP8 GEMM. It costs substantial engineering complexity: custom kernels, an in-switch reduction path that was rolled back once in production, and a four-GPU H100 topology with a dedicated decoder GPU. Failures include numerical risk from FP8 cache quantization (mitigated here by lip-sync validation but not guaranteed on other models), correctness bugs in the delta-rotation path, and fused-kernel instability under production load. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Grounded but Not Immune: Confirmation Bias in Agent-as-a-judge
item.description: This is a diagnostic study rather than a new method: it shows that an Agent-as-a-Judge given tools and full trajectories is not grounded against a single false pre-screening note, which overturns up to 40% of correct verdicts across four judges and five datasets, so it replaces naive trust that tool access alone makes LLM judges reliable. Adoption costs little: keep untrusted pre-screening cues out of judge prompts, apply the paper's lightweight mitigations, and audit judge trajectories for the three classified failure modes (over-trust, hallucination, under-investigation). What can fail after adoption is residual bias, since mitigations blunt but never remove the effect, and smaller judges exhibit spread error modes that are harder to catch than the over-trust pattern dominant in Claude judges. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Agents, Think Only When it Helps
item.description: The method replaces the common practice of distilling complete teacher trajectories with interleaved thoughts and actions by training only on thoughts whose information is not already disclosed in actions. It reduces supervision and training-data cost when thoughts are redundant, while adding the complexity of identifying discrepant cases where thoughts carry unique information. It can fail if informative reasoning is mistakenly treated as redundant and removed, degrading student performance in cases where actions do not reveal the needed information. 0 independent implementations, 20 stars. Research area: distillation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Cognitive Bias Signatures in Search-Equipped LLM Agents: A Stage-Resolved Analysis
item.description: This replaces ad hoc prompting intuition about search-agent reliability with a controlled evaluation harness that isolates evidence-order, dead-end-history, and wrong-hypothesis effects across retrieval, opening, and answer stages. It costs the construction of matched synthetic search worlds and instrumented logging of queries, retrievals, and openings, adding evaluation complexity without a stated production-speed or quality gain. After adoption, its synthetic-world findings may not transfer to real corpora, and the exploratory interventions suggest fixes such as forcing counter-evidence opening can reduce accuracy rather than improve it. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Give the Drafter a Second Chance to Guess: Parallel Reconsideration for Speculative Decoding
item.description: The method replaces the single-pass draft generation of feature-level drafters (e.g., EAGLE-style heads) with a drafting pass plus uncertainty-triggered reconsideration passes, run in parallel, whose refined guesses are appended to the draft tree. It requires a co-designed drafter training recipe and an updated serving-time drafting algorithm, so the cost is retraining or fine-tuning the drafter and modifying the inference stack, while claimed latency overhead is negligible. It can fail if the base model lacks an open checkpoint to train the drafter against (ruling out API-only targets), if the workload's token distribution makes uncertainty estimates poorly calibrated, or if the modest single-digit speedup does not justify the engineering and training effort. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: speculative decoding. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Prospective Memory for Proactive LLM Agents
item.description: Pro-Memory replaces purely retrospective agent memory (conversation history plus retrieval) with a separated store of pending future intentions, each linked to supporting evidence and activation conditions, plus a gating step that decides when an intention becomes actionable and an experience memory distilled from completed episodes. The cost is additional architecture and orchestration: intention-state tracking, per-observation matching against pending goals, and extra LLM calls for activation assessment and episode distillation, all of which add latency, token spend, and implementation complexity. It can fail if activation conditions are mis-specified (missed or premature triggers), if the intention-actionable judgment is unreliable on real workloads, or if the agent's domain has few genuinely delayed intentions, in which case the overhead buys nothing over a simple task list. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: PersonaCodeBench: Evaluating Coding Agents in Persona-driven Human-Interactive Sessions
item.description: The method replaces static, single-turn coding benchmarks with persona-driven, multi-turn evaluation that turns user characteristics into verifiable obligations. It costs a controller, user simulator, requirement specification, and dual verifiers, increasing evaluation complexity and runtime. It can fail if the simulated user or requirement disclosure diverges from real users, and verifier ambiguity can misstate persona fulfillment. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Toward a Compositional Knowledge Architecture for a Shared Organizational Cortex
item.description: It replaces conventional retrieval, knowledge graphs, and agent memory stores that keep raw records but discard the interpretations, justifications, and revision history built on them. The cost is substantial engineering complexity: four persistent layers, a truth-maintenance network, and versioned Dimensions all require schema design, ingestion pipelines, and ongoing curation beyond a standard RAG stack. It can fail if interpretation-entry quality is inconsistent, if the truth-maintenance propagation produces stale or contradictory claim standings, or if the modest retrieval gains do not justify the maintenance burden at small scale. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: retrieval and RAG. Recommendation: test.

item.title: FlyHash for LLM Agent Memory: An Empirical Validation and a New Application
item.description: FlyHash replaces dense-vector embedding stores searched with ANN indexes such as HNSW (and conventional SimHash binary codes) with sparse random-projection plus winner-take-all binary codes for agent memory retrieval. Its cost is practical rather than accuracy-related: at equal bits its codes are larger and slower to compare than SimHash's, and HNSW dominates both hash methods at ordinary scale, with a sparse-set comparison recovering only part of the latency gap. It can fail to deliver any deployment benefit unless the workload is genuinely bit-budget-constrained, since the quality-per-bit advantage does not translate into memory or latency savings against the current default. 2 independent implementations, 1 star. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Item Representations Matter: Bridging Hard Semantic IDs and Soft Prototype Mixtures for Generative Retrieval
item.description: It replaces flat per-item embedding tables and hard quantized Semantic IDs in generative retrieval recommenders with a soft mixture of shared prototypes plus an item-specific residual vector, trained jointly and kept continuous at inference. It costs the additional prototype and assignment parameters, joint training complexity, and tuning of assignment priors, though it avoids a separate quantization tokenizer and can improve inference throughput relative to discrete code decoding. Gains are concentrated on sparse datasets (two Amazon benchmarks) with only a small improvement on Steam, so on dense or well-populated item catalogs the added machinery may not pay off, and pretrained content embeddings or SID priors are needed for the stronger configurations. 0 independent implementations, 30 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Beyond the Agent Harness: Boundary Criteria for Software-Factory Orchestration - A Single-Operator Case Study
item.description: The method replaces ad hoc assignment of mechanisms and failures to agent-harness, factory-harness, or domain layers with explicit operational boundary criteria plus a three-field failure coding scheme. It costs only documentation and coding effort, but adds process overhead and requires disciplined incident logging to be usable. It can fail because the criteria were developed on a single operator's pipeline, model coders left 8-13 of 20 incident fields undetermined and flagged half of all units as ambiguous, and the authors state that coder agreement is neither accuracy nor usefulness. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Octopus: One Brain, Many Branches for Latent-KV Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning
item.description: Octopus replaces multi-agent frameworks that duplicate prefix KV caches per branch, communicate via re-prefilled text summaries, and flatten branch structure during RL, with a single backbone coordinating over a GPU-resident DAG of shared KV pages trained via packed DAG-GRPO. The cost is substantial engineering: custom paged-KV management with fork/mount/rewind primitives, a block-sparse packed attention trainer, and a hybrid full-attention plus linear-recurrent (Gated DeltaNet/Mamba-2) backbone, none of which are available as off-the-shelf serving or training components. Failures include dependence on that specific hybrid architecture (attention-only KV mounting assumes linear-recurrent layers to bypass), possible credit-assignment noise from leave-one-branch-out rewards, and results validated only on sparse BM25 retrieval tasks at 4B scale. 3 independent implementations, 34 stars. Research area: multi-agent orchestration. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Uncertainty calibration in Bayesian M/EEG source imaging
item.description: The framework replaces uncalibrated Bayesian M/EEG source estimates (BMN+sLORETA, SBL) with posterior calibration via isotonic recalibration of credible-region levels using empirical coverage. It costs simulation-based calibration runs and closed-form posterior computation, with complexity in evidence-maximization noise learning and post-hoc recalibration. It can fail through residual miscalibration that persists after recalibration, and transfer of calibration across mismatched SNR, sparsity, or head models is condition dependent. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: other. Recommendation: not applicable.

item.title: LowRAM: Low-Rank Keys and Amortised Values for Composable KV Cache Compression at Test-Time
item.description: LowRAM replaces the full-precision per-token KV cache with cross-layer low-rank keys plus per-head value predictors that store residuals only for poorly reconstructed tokens. It costs a test-time predictor-fitting step during prefill (reducible via meta-learned initialisation), added implementation complexity in the decode path, and a small quality loss that grows with compression ratio. It can fail on workloads where the key-to-value predictability assumption breaks down, on short contexts where cache pressure is irrelevant, and if the reconstruction overhead at each decode step erodes the throughput gain on a single 24 GB GPU. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: KV cache. Recommendation: test.

item.title: NUMA-Torch: Compiler-Driven NUMA-Aware LLM Prefill on Multi-Socket CPUs
item.description: The method replaces standard TorchInductor's NUMA-agnostic weight allocation and kernel scheduling with compiler-level NUMA-aware tensor parallelism that shards weights per socket and pins threads and allocations locally via CPU affinity. It requires a multi-socket CPU-only serving host, a modified TorchInductor toolchain, and weight sharding across sockets, adding compiler and deployment complexity. It can fail or be irrelevant on single-socket machines, on GPU-based serving where DRAM locality across sockets is not the bottleneck, and for operators lacking control over the compiler stack. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: serving and batching. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: DARE: Difficulty Analysis for Repair Enhancement
item.description: The method replaces uniform agent support and difficulty assessment based on solve rates with a framework that uses 151 static features to predict task failure rates and select task-specific support. It costs the engineering complexity of extracting feature groups and the computational expense of initially establishing ground-truth failure rates across multiple agents. It can fail if the moderate correlation (rho = .476-.621) misidentifies task difficulty, leading to mismatched support and suboptimal repair outcomes. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: When File Ingestion Misleads Language Models: Measuring and Mitigating Divergences in Office Documents
item.description: Prism replaces generic document text extractors that either expose hidden OOXML channels or drop visible content and reading order, causing models to see text diverging from what users view. It reconstructs the human-visible view from the OOXML specification before sending text to the model, with lightweight preprocessing overhead and no need to change downstream LLM APIs or infrastructure. What can fail is completeness across document formats or malformed OOXML files; if the reconstruction is imperfect or an extractor changes, hidden channels may still leak or visible content may be lost, so validation against your document types is required. 0 independent implementations, 3 stars. Research area: safety and guardrails. Recommendation: adopt.

item.title: Learning When Human Decisions Matter: Executor-Relative Consultation Value for LLM Agents
item.description: The method replaces ad hoc escalation rules, direct prompting about when to ask a human, and rollout-based value estimation at deployment with offline Monte Carlo executor rollouts distilled into lightweight predictors for budgeted consultation allocation. It costs offline rollout supervision, executor-dependent value estimation, predictor training, and added allocation complexity, while avoiding rollout-based value estimation during deployment. It can fail when the offline executor rollouts do not match the production executor or task distribution, when the human budget or consultation interface changes, or when value predictors misrank rare but high-impact decisions. 0 independent implementations, 20 stars. Research area: planning and decomposition. Recommendation: test.

item.title: A Hybrid Approach for Automated Security Pattern Recovery
item.description: SecPatRec replaces one-shot end-to-end LLM prompting for security pattern recovery with a ReAct-style agent that uses semantic and lexical code search for role detection and grounding, combined with static code property graph analysis for interaction recovery. The approach adds pipeline complexity and requires curated pattern reference architectures plus per-repository static graph construction, though it lowers LLM API costs relative to the baseline and handles repositories exceeding the baseline's input limit. Failures include incorrect role grounding when code search retrieves irrelevant entities, errors in statically derived interaction sequences (the weakest score at 0.66), and dependence on the availability of prescribed pattern role specifications. 0 independent implementations, 8 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Reglos: A Self-Evolving Personal Memory Agent with Recursive Self-Improvement
item.description: Replaces static memory stores and manually tuned retrieval harnesses with an append-only per-user memory whose context-assembly harness is iteratively patched by a coding agent and screened by a cross-family critic for benchmark overfitting. Costs are inference-only (training-free) but substantial: extra coding-agent and critic calls per patch cycle, a frozen evaluator stage, and dependence on a second model family for the critic, all adding latency and API spend. Failure modes include overfitting patches that pass the critic anyway, evaluator lock-in after freezing, memory growth from the append-only record, and gains that may not transfer to the reader's private workloads. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: memory and context. Recommendation: test.

item.title: SBVUL: Statement-Based Vulnerability Detection
item.description: Replaces function-level vulnerable/benign LLM classification with a two-agent pipeline that localizes and confirms exploitable statements using repository exploration and control/data-flow analysis. Costs multiple LLM calls per function (an exploration agent plus a per-candidate confirmation agent), implying significant API spend or infeasible latency on a single 24 GB GPU with open-weight models, and adds agent orchestration complexity. Fails by confirming candidate statements in 23–61% of patched functions and achieving at most 0.315 statement precision, so false positives remain high and the 200-pair benchmark may not transfer to other codebases. 0 independent implementations, 0 stars. Research area: coding agents. Recommendation: test.

item.title: HarnessFlow: MCTS-Guided Harness Optimization for LLM Agents
item.description: HarnessFlow replaces the manual, ad-hoc design of agent scaffolding and tool-use loops with an automated Monte Carlo Tree Search over executable harness code. The approach requires a budget of approximately 15 end-to-end evaluation cycles per task and the operational cost of running a coding agent to generate and test candidate harnesses. Reliance on archived execution history can lead to overfitting to specific benchmarks or failure to generalize to unseen environments, and the MCTS search may converge on suboptimal harness designs if the evaluation budget is too constrained or the coding agent produces buggy code. 1 independent implementation, 23 stars. Research area: tool use. Recommendation: test.

item.title: CLEAR: Structured Specifications for Controllable Long-Horizon ML Research Engineering
item.description: The paper proposes CLEAR, which replaces the implicit, free-form interpretation of research artifacts with structured specifications that an agent maintains while translating papers into executable ML systems. The cost is an additional specification-authoring and maintenance layer on top of agent execution, plus orchestration complexity, with no quantified gain reported in the abstract. It can fail if the specification is wrong or incomplete, if the agent drifts from it during long execution, and because automating full research-to-system workflows typically demands repeated long training and evaluation runs that exceed a single 24 GB GPU and a limited cloud budget. 0 independent implementations, 1 star. Research area: planning and decomposition. Recommendation: watch.

item.title: Scalable Bayesian Gaussian Process Classification for Cancer Histopathology: Calibrated Uncertainty Under Distribution Shift
item.description: The method replaces neural-network and stochastic variational GP classifiers for calibrated pathology prediction by running HMC-based low-rank Gaussian Process Classification on frozen Phikon foundation-model embeddings. It costs the infrastructure to extract embeddings at scale, a low-rank kernel factorization via RPCholesky, and HMC posterior sampling over roughly 300,000 points, which is heavier than a single deterministic classifier and adds implementation and tuning complexity. It can fail when the frozen embeddings are mismatched to a target hospital, when kernel or likelihood choices are poorly specified, or when the low-rank approximation discards structure needed for rare subgroups, despite improved reported calibration. 0 independent implementations, 4 stars. Research area: agent evaluation. Recommendation: test.

item.title: Bayesian Tensor Train Kernel Machines with Automatic Model Complexity Inference
item.description: Replaces deterministic tensor-network kernel machines with manually tuned TT ranks and feature dimensions by inferring both through hierarchical ARD priors and mean-field variational inference. Costs the same asymptotic complexity as deterministic alternating least squares but adds probabilistic bookkeeping, requires an over-parameterized initialization, and remains a kernel machine whose cubic-in-samples scaling persists unless the underlying kernel solver is approximated.
